correctness.rationale: A moving median of affine inputs is continuous, piecewise affine, and away from ties its derivative at output i reads one input derivative h_{a_i} from within the clamped radius-r window. Every h decomposes as a constant plus weighted single jumps 1_{j>=t}; the selected image of a jump is constant 0 to the left of its influence band and 1 to its right, with at most 2r+1 output edges able to alternate. Triangle inequality and line integration yield V(Mx-My)<= (2r+1)V(x-y) for all real pairs, no genericity restriction. At n=2r+2, k=r+1, the interleaved baseline x=(0,2,...,2k-2,1,3,...,2k-1) has median output i; adding epsilon 1_{i>=k} makes output changes alternate 0/epsilon on all 2r+1 edges, proving equality. Appending endpoint baseline repetitions and perturbation ones preserves all original changes at larger n. For shorter paths, at most n-1<2r+1 output edges can change for a single jump, and the same selector decomposition gives a strict upper bound. Independently checked witnesses through r=31, boundary extension and sample exact pairs; no finite census is used as the universal proof.

value.rationale: Running medians are classical one-signal total-variation smoothers; their full-window amplification of differences is a substantial counterintuitive stability threshold. The theorem supplies the complete all-radii large-path exact law, optimal first path length 2r+2 and explicit rank-selector witnesses, not merely another radius-one or cyclic instance. It is a natural all-window invariant that matters in nonlinear robust filtering.

final_claim: For every integer r>=1 and every clamped finite path with n>=2r+2 vertices, the centered width-(2r+1) running median has attained sharp two-input adjacent-TV coefficient 2r+1. The smallest length achieving this full factor is n=2r+2.
limitations: All-radii claim holds for n>=2r+2 with repeated endpoint padding and unweighted noncyclic adjacent TV; shorter path exact norms not determined.
No cyclic, mirror-reflected, weighted-median or higher-order-statistic generalization.
